evidence.finding: Reject null output=4, existing process singleton=0xE and API selector other than1/2=7. Read setting type3, vim.registry0404 or vim.registry0500; require matching PassThruSupport.04.04/.05.00 prefix; query HKLM selected key FunctionLibrary/Vendor/Name. Construct CJ2534v2 then vtable+34 (04.04) or+78 (05.00) open; on open failure destroy/reset singleton and return error. Registry/config/allocation failures are not an automatic device retry.
No singleton=>8. Invoke vtable+38 close, obtain last error on7, then deleting destructor and singleton reset regardless of returned close status.

For API1 with exact Vendor DENSO CORPORATION and Name TIS Techstream VIM load physical DLL directly (LoadLibraryW). Otherwise load install-directory ptshim32.dll/API1 or ptshim32_0500.dll/API2 with LoadLibraryExW(flags8), call PassThruLoadLibrary(physical FunctionLibrary path), create save/finish/stop events and logger worker. Logger insertion is deliberate controller routing, not DLL-search-path replacement.

Require API1 and loaded module; already-open byte+5C returns0xE. Resolve/call PassThruOpen(name,&deviceID); only success stores ID at+78 and sets open+5C. Missing DLL/export or open failure returns7 with stored last-error text.

API2 uses PassThruScanForDevices(&count), then exactly one PassThruGetNextDevice call; parses its device name and calls PassThruOpen("J2534-2:%s",&deviceID). Empty parsed name returns0x22; open success stores+78 and+5C. This body does not iterate all discovered devices.

Require API1/module/open+5C and channel+5D clear (8/0x14 otherwise). Validate flag masks and protocol IDs. Non-DENSO custom0x1000C becomesISO15765(6),0x1000D becomesISO9141(3); direct DENSO IDs gain0x10000. Zero baud defaults:1/3/4=10400,2=41600,5/6/0x1000B/0x8012/0x1000C=500000,0x8005=125000,0x8013=0. Call physical PassThruConnect(device,protocol,flags,baud,&channel), store+74; for applicable legacy protocols install PASS_FILTER defaults. Failure attempts controller disconnect before connected+5D is set; its guard returns2 without calling physical PassThruDisconnect. Thus a physical channel may remain despite setup failure until later driver/device close. Channel+5D is set only on successful setup.

Require API1/module/open/channel. Call physical PassThruDisconnect(channel); even if it fails, clear tracked filters and default-filter flag+7C, flag bytes+7E/+7F/+80 and connected+5D. Return driver status; software disconnected does not prove hardware acknowledged disconnect. Missing PassThruDisconnect export returns7 BEFORE cleanup, preserving+5D/list/flags; only a driver invocation reaches unconditional resets. Numeric channel+74 is never zeroed. Exceptional direct-DENSO path: driver status7 and+7D set resolves GetLastError; if absent, code logs FUNC_ADDRESS_FAILED but still calls null before software resets. Thus unconditional post-invocation reset describes normally returning paths, not this fault.

Require loaded module and open+5C. If connected, disconnect via API-specific path; then PassThruClose(deviceID). Only success clears+5C and deviceID and calls save-log vtable+B0; close failure returns7 and preserves open bookkeeping until destruction. Disconnect status is ignored. Missing disconnect export can preserve+5D even after Close success; Open then sets only+5C/+78, so API04 next Connect can still reject14. A failed Close leaves+5C=1: Open rejectsE while Connect can proceed if+5D cleared. Finalize destroys regardless and destructor attempts another physical Close while+5C remains set; repeated error does not prove hardware leak.

Read selected API04 registry metadata. Probe up to11 registry-supported protocol IDs by connect/disconnect through live singleton. Exact DENSO/TIS pair yields device kind1 or4 (probe success); other vendors2 or8. This is a device-capability probe, not a pure registry enumeration operation.

Read selected API05 registry metadata and ETHERNET capability; probe protocol0x800F at100000000 baud with resource parameters, disconnect afterward, return device kind8 on success else2. Registry metadata alone is not proof the channel opens.

Wait indefinitely for stop or SAVE_J2534_LOG_FILE_EVENT; on save reset event, call save-log vtable+B0, signal FINISH_J2534_LOG_FILE_EVENT and return to wait. Finish signals completion of the attempt, not necessarily successful persistence.

For non-direct-DENSO route resolve PassThruSaveLog. Read common setting type1 path.productFolder; prefix CSIDL0x2E, append ErrorReport/j2534_MMDDYYYYhhmmss.log using GetLocalTime and call shim save. Current filename policy is settings-backed; hard-coded legacy Techstream directory is not the current source of truth. Provider errors return7/A0040005/C0040102. Both current shipped shim SaveLog bodies are no-op success; this requested pathname does not establish that a file is created.

Validate NIC/address pointers and two-byte logical source address. Read ethernet.connectIPTimeout from setting type1; WSAStartup2.2; UDP socket(AF_INET,SOCK_DGRAM,UDP), exclusive-address and broadcast options. Poll SIO_GET_INTERFACE_LIST for selected NIC IPv4/up state at1000ms until timeout. Vehicle-ID discovery precedes TCP bind(selectedIPv4,port0), connect(peer,13400), and15-byte routing-activation request(type0005,length7). Require response type0006,length>=5 and matching tester source-address echo; this body does not check the activation-response status byte. Many early errors return with global sockets/WSA state still allocated; caller must execute teardown. Direct repeated NDISConnect has no existing-socket/startup guard: WSAStartup and newly created UDP/TCP handles overwrite process globals. Normal ChangeCommIF failure invokes KGP NDIS disconnect override even when+0C=0, closing partial globals; bypassing that owner is not equivalent. No allocation-liveness conclusion follows solely from omitted calls.
shutdown(SD_BOTH) and close TCP; close UDP; WSACleanup if startup succeeded. Log but suppress cleanup failures, invalidate socket globals, clear protocol-version/NIC/address globals, always return0.

Require two-byte source/target logical addresses, nonempty bounded payload and TCP socket. Clear stale TCP receive buffer, build DoIP type8001 with four address bytes and length(payload+4), send once and await diagnostic acknowledgment. Return send/ack error, no transparent resend.

Read TCP header then body, require type8001,length>=4 and caller capacity>=length-4. Validate source/target match last send, copy diagnostic bytes after four logical-address bytes, return actual payload length. Timeout=>0x8003, EOF/socket error=>0x8017, address mismatch=>0x8002, invalid length/type=>0x8000. Header and body each accumulate positive short recv results to exact requested size; WinsockLogger does not parse. Invalid type/too-small length/caller-capacity rejection consumes header only, leaving body queued; partial-body timeout consumes bytes with no persistent assembly state for next call. Neither version/inverse bytes nor fixed global scratch capacityFFFF are checked against declared length before body recv; caller payload capacity is not a scratch-buffer bound. High-bit lengths reach signed-positive helper check8005 when caller capacity passes.

Bind UDP to selected NIC and supplied source port; broadcast 8-byte vehicle-ID request FF00000100000000 to255.255.255.255 at the supplied port. Clear stale UDP input first. On ReceiveVehicleIdMessage timeout0x8001 retry once (two requests total); all other failures return immediately.

select/recvfrom within supplied timeout, skip self-originated packets, accept datagram length>=40 and payload type0004; remember sender IPv4 and protocol-version byte. VIN/EID/GID identity is not checked in this function.

Read8-byte TCP header and declared body; allow types8002/8003 with nonzero body>=4, match reversed source/target addresses. Type8003=>0x8000;8002 succeeds. WSAETIMEDOUT10060=>0x8003, EOF/other recv errors=>0x8017; address mismatch=>0x8002. Positive short reads are accumulated separately for header/body; declared body is read into shared FFFF-byte scratch without an explicit maximum check. Version/inverse and ACK code byte are not checked. A four-byte address-only8002 body succeeds;8003 fails regardless of code. Rejected header does not drain body, and timeout/EOF does not close socket or retain partial parser state.

Require module/open/channel. Replace controller-created default filters with Ioctl10(CLEAR_MSG_FILTERS); invoke real PassThruStartMsgFilter with mask/pattern/flow. Track real driver filterID in an internal linked list, expose a controller-local index as returned filterID. Failures return driver/error status; no retry loop.

If still open call PassThruClose and clear open/channel bytes. Close communication-log handle. Non-direct-DENSO route calls PassThruUnloadLibrary, signals worker stop, waits5000ms then TerminateThread if wait is not signaled; closes four worker/event handles. FreeLibrary physical/shim module and free filter list.

API2/module/open required, but unlike API04 there is no connected+5D rejection or default-filter setup. Forward explicit device/resource/output arguments. Success replaces last physical channel+74 and sets+5D; failure preserves prior+74/+5D. Multiple physical API05 channels are therefore not represented by a channel-count flag.

API2/module/open required; does not require connected+5D. Resolve and invoke physical disconnect for the supplied channel even when+5D=0, then clear+5D regardless of driver result. Missing export returns7 without clearing flags. Does not erase+74 or clear API04 filter list/translation flags.

API2/module/open required, but no connected+5D gate. Call driver ReadMsgs with original byte-count/message pointers and timeout; optional logging afterward, no DoIP reassembly. API05 stream fulfillment belongs to the selected external FunctionLibrary, not this wrapper.

Complete address-value comparator: first compare length at+8, then every byte. False means equality, true means different. ACK/diagnostic receiver compare two-byte wire source with cached sent target and wire target with cached sent source; no wildcard match.

API1/module/open and connected+5D=1 required; failed setup or failed disconnect followed by clear flag returns2 before driver ReadMsgs. Successful read consumes sticky+7E/+7F/+80 translation flags to mask RxStatus80/100/180000; custom1000C mode+84 changes status handling. Generic connect only sets requested translation bytes, not clears unrequested ones; a failed-connect retry can inherit them until an actually executed disconnect or destruction.
API2/module/open guard then tail-dispatch physical driver LogicalConnect with caller stack unchanged. Does not update+5D/+74 or track logical IDs. KGP owns IP4/UDP/TCP slots2240/2244/2248.
API2/module/open guard then tail-dispatch physical driver LogicalDisconnect, no ID/flag bookkeeping. KGP backend zeros every supplied logical slot after attempted driver teardown even on error.

Resolve installed J2534Ctrl.dll with LoadLibraryExW(flags8), call Initialize(API,&deviceID,null), map nonzero status with0x91010000, set log-collection mode and load-version/device fields, initialize disconnected CONNECT_INFO. Load/export failures=>C0040301/C0040302.
Same loader, but Initialize third argument is J2534-2:. Used for Ethernet/extended bus routes; this is not equivalent to automatically selecting API05.

App bus low nibble selects transport class independently of category-byte low5 support/session family. Reuse only when bus/addressing/mode/category compatibility checks pass. Incompatible CAN11/29/FD, legacy or Ethernet transitions stop communication, Disconnect and sometimes FinalizeDevice; create/reinitialize selected protocol object. P5 low5=14/15/16 gates session cleanup separately; low5=16 forces additional finalize when changing family. Compatible reuse exits without a new physical Connect; cached bus/category, WWH and OBD-on-UDS modes and FD ECU identity gate reuse. Any backend-connect error flows Disconnect(0): ordinary base skips physical disconnect if+0C was never set; NDIS override always calls backend teardown.

Select same protocol class from CONNECT_INFO bus low nibble, but adopt caller-supplied device/protocol/channel state through SetConnectParameterGeneral instead of opening a new ordinary channel. Setup error calls Disconnect; special device checks reject VIM-only incompatibilities with90020204.

Optionally stop keepalive first; P5/P6 cleanup invokes stop/default-session paths, then protocol disconnect and deleting destructor. Clear protocol pointer,bus,ECU,current-session and reset timeout10000. Device kinds1/4 additionally FinalizeDevice; other devices can remain open for reconnect.
Call J2534CtrlFinalize if export exists but ignore its result; FreeLibrary and clear module/device/load-version fields. Returns0.
If module exists, Disconnect(1) if protocol object, then FinalizeDevice if still loaded, and reset CONNECT_INFO to no connection. Returns0.

If KGP connected+0C, dispatch disconnect first but ignore its result. Driver connect callback+2144 writes channel+8; set protocol+20D8 even on error, set+0C only on success. Failure maps91010000. KGP and CJ2534 connected flags are distinct; an API04 filter failure leaves both clear even after driver-created numeric ID.

If KGP connected+0C=0 return0 without driver call or clearing channel+8. Otherwise stop services, invoke bound controller disconnect+2148, clear channel/ECU/service/connected fields even on nonzero result, return mapped error. Next ordinary connect can invoke driver again; an absent cleanup call does not prove external hardware allocation survives.
Vtable+120 setter stores supplied numeric channel at protocol object+08; no driver call or ownership flag.
Vtable+128 setter stores supplied protocol at protocol object+20D8; no driver call.

Parallel DS-4 controller has the same API1/2 selected-registry configuration and device singleton contract, protected by process-local critical section. This is a different source/build, not a byte-identical GTSPlus copy. Unlike main, failed post-constructor API04/API05 Open returns without deleting/resetting singleton 100287E0. Next Initialize returnsE until explicit Finalize; KGP Open failure calls CloseDevice, which finalizes this retained singleton. Do not transfer main failed-open reset to DS-4.
Under the DS-4 critical section, close via vtable38, retain returned status, destroy singleton and reset it; missing singleton returns8. No NDIS exports exist in this installed DS-4 controller.

DS-4 API04 shares late+5D commit and guarded rollback: physical connect success stores+74, missing/default-filter failure calls disconnect while+5D=0, so no physical disconnect occurs. Subsequent API04 connect is permitted and overwrites+74 on success. DS-4 generic flags80/100 set+7E/+7F without clearing absent bits; custom-mode dword is+80 (main uses+84). No main-only8012/8013 cases.

DS-4 API1/module/open/channel guards; missing export preserves bookkeeping. After driver invocation, clear filter list,+7C,+7E/+7F,+5D despite driver failure, retain numeric+74 and custom-mode+80. Main additionally clears translation byte+80, whose role differs in DS-4. Exceptional direct-DENSO path: driver status7 and+7D set resolves GetLastError; if absent, code logs FUNC_ADDRESS_FAILED but still calls null before software resets. Thus unconditional post-invocation reset describes normally returning paths, not this fault.

Same close ordering as main with DS-4 vtable slots: if+5D set, API04 guarded disconnect or API05 direct physical disconnect; ignore disconnect status. Then physical Close; success clears only open+5C/device+78 and calls save slot+B4; failure maps7 and preserves open/device. Missing disconnect export can leave+5D set even after successful Close. Next connect then fails open gate8, not a hardware observation.
DS-4 API05 matches main API05: no already-connected rejection; physical Connect success replaces last+74/sets+5D, failure preserves these. No default-filter setup.
DS-4 API05 matches main: call supplied channel even if+5D=0; clear+5D after invocation regardless of status. Missing export or unopened device returns without state reset.

DS-4 API05 forwards ReadMsgs unchanged after API/module/open gates, even with+5D=0. No short-read accumulation in controller; only optional log callback. KGP requests exact stream-byte counts, so external driver must fulfill each requested block or KGP reports short response.
API2/module/open guard then tail-dispatch physical driver LogicalConnect with caller stack unchanged. Does not update+5D/+74 or track logical IDs. KGP owns IP4/UDP/TCP slots2240/2244/2248.
API2/module/open guard then tail-dispatch physical driver LogicalDisconnect, no ID/flag bookkeeping. KGP backend zeros every supplied logical slot after attempted driver teardown even on error.

Pass response to protocol classifier:90020323 loops pending until180000ms;90020326 requeues cached request while counter<100(hex), then exits; other classifier errors returned. ERR_BUFFER_EMPTY10 maps91010009; short/type/source errors remain distinct. Timing comes from Ethernet DB rows; no blanket infinite retry. Chunk limit1020 is HEX (4128 bytes), not decimal1020. Version/inverse and logical destination are unchecked. Classifier runs on first body block; success then source comparison precedes later raw chunk concatenation. Driver ReadMsgs and shim supply byte-stream fulfillment; host TCP fragmentation loop is absent in this DS-4 route.
